title: Weak equivalences form an accessible arrow subcategory
statement: Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category with the conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]; no simplicial enrichment is required here. A category is locally presentable if it is cocomplete and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa$, generated under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects $P$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves these colimits. Here $\kappa$-filtered means every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms admits a cocone, and regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of cardinality less than $\kappa$ has cardinality less than $\kappa$. Suppose $\mathcal M$ is combinatorial: its underlying category is locally presentable and each of its two weak factorization systems is generated by a small set of arrows, meaning the right class is precisely the maps admitting diagonal fillers against that set. Let $W\subseteq\mathcal M^{[1]}$ be the full subcategory on weak equivalences, with commuting squares as morphisms. A replete full subcategory $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D$ is an accessible subcategory if, for some infinite regular $\lambda$, it is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits computed in $\mathcal D$ and is generated under those colimits by a small set of its objects. Replete means closed under isomorphism in $\mathcal D$. Then $W$ is an accessible subcategory of $\mathcal M^{[1]}$. In particular this includes closure under sufficiently filtered colimits in the ambient arrow category, not just abstract accessibility of $W$.
